back: Communicating over a distance using electrical signals, light or radio waves.
Microphone (sound → electrical) → encoded as digital → aerial sends radio waves → base station → network → base station → receiving aerial → decoded → loudspeaker (electrical → sound).

Battery: chemical → electrical. Microphone: sound → electrical. Sending aerial: electrical → radio waves. Receiving aerial: radio waves → electrical. Loudspeaker: electrical → sound. Screen: electrical → light.
The area served by one base station. As a phone moves, the call is handed over from one base station to the next.
Encoded as digital data → internet (radio, cables, fibres) → mail server → stored in the inbox → downloaded and decoded by the receiver's device.
Only 0 and 1 must be told apart, so noise can be removed and the signal regenerated: clear over long distances.
Both carry electrical signals in copper. Twisting reduces interference (cheap, short distances); coaxial has a metal screen (well shielded, more information).
Pulses of light kept in a glass core by total internal reflection. Huge capacity, low loss, no electrical interference, hard to tap; but expensive and fragile.
Radio waves between a wireless router and devices. No cables and devices can move; but short range, weakened by walls, needs a password.
